Most lifters aiming to build or keep muscle land somewhere around 0.7 to 1 gram of protein per pound of bodyweight a day (roughly 1.6 to 2.2 g per kg). Research suggests gains level off near the top of that range, so eating far more than that doesn't buy you much.

Spreading it across 3 to 5 meals works well, with a solid protein serving at each. Eating enough total food matters just as much, since protein can't do its job if you're underfed overall.

If you have a medical condition or kidney concerns, check with a doctor or dietitian for what's right for you. Want me to pull up some high-protein recipes?
